## Step 1 · The total of each group: a PivotTable {.study}

{{< watch title="Create a PivotTable" source="Microsoft Support" url="https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/excel/get-started/create-a-pivottable-to-analyze-worksheet-data" length="0:45" checked="2026-10-31" captions="English" >}}

- A long list has many rows. You want **one total for each group** (each
  type, each department).
- A **PivotTable** does it in a few clicks: **Insert › PivotTable › OK**.
- Tick the group (text): it goes to **Rows**. Tick the number: it goes to
  **Values** (Sum).
- The **Grand Total** is the total of the whole list.

::: {.callout-note title="Model · Rana's sales"}
Rana has her sales of one week in a list (made up). She wants the total of
each type. PivotTable: Rows **Type**, Values **Sum of Total**. Paper 206
JD, Drinks 71 JD, Bags 78 JD; Grand Total 355 JD.
:::

## Step 2 · What the data shows, and a chart {.study}

{{< watch title="Create charts" source="Microsoft Support" url="https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/excel/get-started/create-a-chart-from-start-to-finish" length="0:52" checked="2026-10-31" captions="English" >}}

- Read the PivotTable: **which group is the biggest**? Which is the
  smallest? Is one group **more than half** of the total?
- A true sentence about the data, with a number, helps a manager decide.
- A **column chart** compares the groups: select the totals with the
  headings (not the Grand Total), then **Insert › Column › Clustered
  Column**, and click **Chart Title** to type a title.

::: {.callout-note title="Model · What Rana's sales show"}
Paper 206 of 355 JD: more than half of the money. So Rana orders more
paper. The column of Paper in the chart is the tallest.
:::

## Step 3 · AI adds a total to your sheet {.study}

- On **tutudocs.com** (free, **no sign-in**) you open your Excel file in
  the browser.
- Click **AI Assistant** and ask for **one change**, for example: *Add a
  row at the end: Total, with the sum of the Total column.*
- **File › Download**, the choice that ends in **.xlsx**: the new file
  opens in Excel.

## Tasks to submit {.tasks}

Open the start file `training.xlsx`: the training hours of the Sunrise
staff (12 rows).

### Task 1 · A PivotTable and a chart

1. Make a PivotTable: Rows **Department**, Values **Sum of Hours**.
   (Step 1 shows how.)
2. Insert a **column chart** of the totals, with the title *Training
   hours*. (Step 2 shows how.)
3. Save the file as `training.xlsx`.

### Task 2 · Two answers

::: {.pick}
**a)** Which department has the most hours?

- Sales
- Office
- Shop
:::

::: {.pick}
**b)** Make a second PivotTable with Rows **Course**. Which sentence is true?

- Safety has more hours than Word
- Half of all the hours are Excel
- Word has the most hours
:::

### Task 3 · AI adds a total

1. On **tutudocs.com**, open the **start file** `training.xlsx` (the one
   you downloaded, without the PivotTable).
2. Ask the AI Assistant: *Add a row at the end: Total, with the sum of the
   Hours column.* Download it (the choice that ends in .xlsx). (Step 3
   shows how.)
3. Open the new file in Excel and save it as `training-ai.xlsx`.

*Submit:* `training.xlsx` and `training-ai.xlsx`.
